# FEAT-03 (FR-RPT-01) implementation plan

This round is **PLAN ONLY**: no files were modified, no dependencies were installed, nothing was committed, and no branch was switched.

## 1. Current branch, commit and working-tree status

- Branch: `CS5351` (tracking `origin/CS5351`); no branch was created or switched.
- Commit: `d0ca820925f959163d9fcc731c6376caee7afc75` (`test(FEAT-02): record live semantic evaluation runs...`).
- Working tree: clean (`git status --porcelain` produced no output).
- The baseline commit `4cff72b` exists and can be used for diff review.
- Note: in `test/offline/test_instrument_identity.py` the patch target is `tradingagents.dataflows.vendors.yahoo.market.yf.Ticker`, while `get_company_profile` lives in `yahoo/fundamentals.py`. Both reference the same `yfinance` module object, so it currently works; new tests should patch the `fundamentals` module to avoid relying on that coincidence.

## 2. Completion criteria (mapped to FR-RPT-01)

| No. | Completion criterion | Acceptance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| C1 | Each consolidated report has exactly one `Company Background` section | RPT-T1/T2/T3; markdown count = 1, HTML `<section>` count = 1 |
| C2 | It sits after the header and before the analyst reports (`## I. Analyst Team Reports`) | Position assertions in RPT-T1/T2/T3 |
| C3 | It is independent of analyst selection; no Fundamentals Analyst required | RPT-T1 runs the full graph with `selected_analysts` not containing `fundamentals` |
| C4 | Show the available name/industry/a 1–2 sentence business description; omit missing fields | RPT-T1 (all fields), RPT-T2 (name only) |
| C5 | When no usable fields exist, show an unavailable notice and complete the export | RPT-T3 (the final decision still appears in the export) |
| C6 | Historical dates follow the existing policy: the current name must be explicitly labelled as current; undated industry/business description must not be presented as historical fact | RPT-T4 |
| C7 | Markdown and HTML show the same information | All cases assert equivalence across both formats |
| C8 | No new agent or model call; reuse the existing data access and export paths | When data retrieval fails or is missing, no model call; baseline tests stay passing |
| C9 | Preserve public imports, CLI, data formats, graph behavior, old-state compatibility | Regression tests + old-state (no new field) cases |

## 3. Actual call paths

**Python entry**: `TradingAgentsGraph.propagate()` → `_run_graph()` → `create_run_state()` → `propagator.create_initial_state()` (`src/tradingagents/graph/propagation.py:13`). `create_run_state` calls `resolve_instrument_context()` (`trading_graph.py:305`), which calls `resolve_instrument_identity()` (`:127`) and finally `get_company_profile()` (`dataflows/vendors/yahoo/fundamentals.py:169`, reading `yf.Ticker(...).info`). The identity result (`company_name/sector/industry/exchange/quote_type`) is retained via `_identity`'s `lru_cache` (`agents/context.py:85`) and is written only in **text form** into the `instrument_context` string; the graph state does not store a structured profile. Then `_run_graph` → `record_decision()` → `save_reports()` (`trading_graph.py:277`) → `write_report_tree()` → optional `render_report()`.

**CLI entry**: `run_analysis()` (`src/cli/run.py:99`) → `create_run_state()` (`:219`, the same identity resolution) → `stream_run` → merge `final_state` → `record_decision` → `_offer_reports()` (`:388/426`) → `graph.save_reports()` → `write_report_tree()`. The CLI terminal display is `display_complete_report(final_state)` (`display.py:383`), which is **not** part of the "consolidated report" export path.

**Current field status**:
- At export time **no** profile is used: `_report_parts()` reads only report/debate state (`reporting.py:77`), and `_header()` writes only the title and run metadata. So the current report has **no** Company Background section.
- Industry: used by `build_instrument_context` on **current-date** runs; suppressed on historical runs (`context.py:138-155`).
- Business description: the `info` returned by `get_company_profile` should contain Yahoo's `longBusinessSummary`, but `_identity` currently does not retain it, so **no path uses it**.
- Filtering/semantics: only `_clean_identity_value` filters whitespace and `none/n/a/nan/null`; historical-date semantics are driven solely by `is_historical()` (`date_window.py:40`).
- `fundamentals.py:get_fundamentals()` is fully suppressed on historical dates via `withhold_live_profile`, so it cannot be used to obtain the profile.

## 4. Recommended design (current vs. proposed)

**Profile ownership (single owner)**
- Add a pure function `company_profile_view(trade_date) -> dict` in `agents/context.py`: it takes the current `identity` (reusing `resolve_instrument_identity`, adding no data access) and returns an **already-filtered, date-marked** field view:
  - Current run (`is_historical` false): `name` (unlabelled), `industry`, `business_description` (trimmed to 1–2 sentences).
  - Historical run: only `name`, with `name_is_current=True`; `industry`, `business_description` **omitted** (because they carry no historical date and cannot stand as historical fact).
- A missing field is simply missing; if all three are empty, return an empty view and let the export layer produce the unavailable notice.
- Extend `_identity` to retain `business_description` (source `longBusinessSummary`, cleaned the same way). This extension is used only for export and **does not change agent prompts**.
- Ownership: `context.py` owns the profile semantics (`_clean_identity_value`, `company_profile_view`); `reporting.py` owns rendering/layout; `report_html.py` only consumes the view provided by `reporting`.

**Field/date semantics**
- "Current name": a historical run outputs an explicit label such as `Name: X (current name; on {date} it may have been named differently)`.
- Industry/business description: must not appear on a historical run (consistent with the existing `build_instrument_context` and `withhold_live_profile` policy).
- Business description: keep only 1–2 sentences (split at sentence-ending punctuation and truncate), and escape for Markdown/HTML.

**Failure handling**
- Profile resolution is fail-open by design (exception → `{}`); at export, when `{}`, output the unavailable notice text (e.g. `Company background is unavailable for this run: no company name, industry or business description was available.`) and continue writing the complete report.
- A missing profile does not change the exit code, rating or graph behavior.

**Old state/compatibility**
- At export, **compute** the view from `trade_date` rather than depending on a new state field, so old JSON logs or an old `final_state` also get a consistent background section. Do not add a required state key.
- Both the `propagate`/CLI entries already put `trade_date` into the state, so `save_reports(final_state,...)` can read it.

**Rendering approach (recommended, minimal intrusion)**
- `reporting.py`: add `_company_background(final_state) -> str` (Markdown); insert that block after `_header()` and before the `## ` groups. Omit missing fields; return a notice paragraph if all are missing. The consolidated report structure is header → Company Background → `## I...`.
- `report_html.py`: insert a `section` after the masthead and before the sections, using the same backing data (`company_profile_view`); do not change agent body rendering. Keep Markdown and HTML sharing one source.
- Note: do not fold the background section into the `_SECTIONS` numbering (to avoid disturbing I–V and the contents/reading experience); present it as an independent block that satisfies "after the header, before the analyst reports, exactly one".

**Relationship to FEAT-05**: the background section is generated at export and does not enter the debate inputs, consistent with FEAT-05's "company background added at export falls outside the debate inputs".

## 5. Proposed editable paths, frozen paths, affected interfaces

**Proposed editable (pending approval)**
| Path | Change | Necessity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/tradingagents/agents/context.py` | `_identity` retains `business_description`; add `company_profile_view()` | Single point owning profile filtering/date semantics; adds no network access |
| `src/tradingagents/reporting.py` | Insert the background block after `_header`; add a private constructor | The single export-layout point, shared by both entries |
| `src/tradingagents/report_html.py` | Insert a background section after the masthead, same source as Markdown | Both formats consistent |
| `test/offline/test_reporting.py` / `test_report_html.py` or a new `test_company_background.py` | RPT-T1..T4 | Verification constraints |
| `.agent/rules.md` and similar governance/docs (optional) | Record an ADR or evidence | Subject to approval |

**Proposed frozen (must not change)**
- `src/tradingagents/dataflows/vendors/yahoo/fundamentals.py` (reuse the existing `get_company_profile`; a read-only reference is acceptable, but leaving it untouched is preferred)
- `src/tradingagents/dataflows/date_window.py` (reuse `is_historical`)
- `src/tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py`, `propagation.py`, `agents/state.py` (do not add a state field)
- `src/cli/run.py`, `src/cli/display.py` (CLI export goes through `save_reports`, so no change needed; the terminal full-report display is outside the consolidated-report scope)
- The CSS/security policy and logo logic of `src/tradingagents/report_html.py`
- Existing FEAT-01/02/05 test files

**Affected interfaces (unchanged or read-only extension)**
- Public: `write_report_tree(final_state, ticker, save_path, settings, html)`, `render_report(...)`, `TradingAgentsGraph.save_reports(...)` signatures unchanged.
- New private functions (`company_profile_view`, `_company_background`) are not public API.
- The `_identity` return dict gains a `business_description` key (backward compatible; added only, not changed).

**Risk/permission note**: `docs/architecture/permission-model.md` is empty; the role allowlist and acceptance cases remain **team-unapproved** suggestions and must not be treated as approved.

## 6. Tests (mapped to RPT-T1..T4, fixed inputs and expectations)

> All offline; no model calls (`Conftest` blocks the network). The profile is fixed as a fixture dict, injected via patching `resolve_instrument_identity` or `_identity`; export goes through `write_report_tree` (both formats) and `TradingAgentsGraph.save_reports` (Python entry); the CLI entry asserts `complete_report.md/html` through `_offer_reports`/`save_reports`.

- **RPT-T1 (FR-RPT-01)**: `selected_analysts=("market","news")` (no fundamentals), profile=`{company_name:"NVIDIA Corporation", industry:"Semiconductors", business_description:"NVIDIA designs GPUs. It also sells networking gear."}`, `trade_date=today`. Expect: one Company Background each in markdown and HTML, after the header and before `## I.` / the first section; both formats contain the name, industry and two-sentence description; an old state without the field also exports. **Covers both entries and both formats.**
- **RPT-T2**: profile only `{company_name:"...", industry:""}`. Expect: only the name shown; other fields absent; the report exports successfully and the final decision is still present.
- **RPT-T3 (negative)**: profile=`{}` (or all cleaned to empty), `fundamentals` not selected, `final_trade_decision` present. Expect: one unavailable notice in each format; the final decision and other sections still export; **no model call occurs** (assert with a counting stub).
- **RPT-T4 (historical)**: `trade_date="2024-05-10"` (< today), profile contains `company_name/industry/business_description`. Expect: the name explicitly labelled "current name"; industry and business description **both absent**; both formats consistent.
- **Boundary negative**: historical + no name but with industry/business description → view empty → unavailable notice, and undated content must not leak.
- **Format consistency**: RPT-T1's visible text is equivalent in `complete_report.md` and `complete_report.html` (after stripping tags).

## 7. Verification commands (plan vs. executed)

**Executed (read-only planning)**
- `git branch --show-current` / `git log --oneline -5` / `git status --porcelain=v1 -b` / `git rev-parse HEAD`: run; see section 1.
- Code and docs search (read/grep): run.

**Planned (not run)**

  - or `python -m pytest test/offline/test_reporting.py test/offline/test_report_html.py -q`
- Full previous offline regression: `python -m pytest -q` (target record: after FEAT-02 the baseline was `1483 passed, 6 skipped, 4 deselected, 100 subtests passed`; this round must only add, not remove)
- Structural check: `ruff check src test`
- Layering constraint: `python -m pytest test/offline/test_layering.py -q` (ensure no vendor library is introduced outside the data layer)
- Targeted structural check for this change: `python -m pytest test/offline/test_instrument_identity.py test/offline/test_undated_tools_as_of.py test/offline/test_options_analyst.py -q` (confirm existing identity/historical/options behavior does not regress)

## 8. Ordered implementation steps and human decisions needed

**Steps (after approval)**
1. `context.py`: `_identity` additionally retains `business_description`; implement `company_profile_view(trade_date)` (filter empty/placeholder; historical shows name only and labels it; business description trimmed to 1–2 sentences); write unit tests first (RPT-T4 + the historical-no-name negative).
2. `reporting.py`: add `_company_background`, inserted after `_header`; omit missing fields, notice if all missing. Test RPT-T1/T2/T3 (markdown).
3. `report_html.py`: insert a same-source section after the masthead; test both-format consistency (RPT-T1) and HTML single-section count.
4. Both entries: `write_report_tree`, `TradingAgentsGraph.save_reports`, and `_offer_reports(save=True)` once each.
5. Historical regressions: `test_instrument_identity.py`, `test_undated_tools_as_of.py`, `test_options_analyst.py`, `test_reporting.py`, `test_report_html.py`.
6. Full `python -m pytest -q` + `ruff check src test`, record evidence and any human interventions to the review memo / trace-matrix.

**Shared-file conflicts (need coordination)**
- `reporting.py` is also modified by FEAT-01 (options section) and FEAT-05 (citation labels); `report_html.py` is used by FEAT-05/06. All three touch the `_header`-adjacent location, so merges must be serialized to avoid overwriting.
- `agents/context.py` is in focus for FEAT-05 (identity context); the `_identity` extension must keep old keys unchanged.
- The test files `test_reporting.py` and `test_report_html.py` are shared with other features; **creating** a new `test_company_background.py` is recommended to reduce conflicts.

**Specific decisions needing human review**
1. Presentation of the background section: independent block (recommended, no disruption to I–V numbering) vs. numbered "0/VI". I recommend the independent block.
2. Whether a historical run may allow "current name only" as the background (RPT-T4 expects this to be allowed and labelled); whether this fits the team's definition of "naming" as identity vs. fact.
3. Business-description source: use Yahoo `longBusinessSummary` (recommended, reuse existing `info`); whether an additional vendor or cache is needed.
4. The truncation rule for the 1–2 sentence business description (sentence-end punctuation counting, handling of abnormally long sentences).
5. The fixed English wording and localization of the unavailable notice (whether `output_language` affects it).
6. Whether `fundamentals.py` may be left untouched (recommended) — reuse only via `get_company_profile`.
7. Test file location: new vs. appended to the existing report tests.
8. Whether `company_profile_view` is exported publicly (recommend keeping it module-private/testable), or exposed via `__all__`/public imports.
9. Performance/cache: reuse `_identity`'s `lru_cache` so export makes zero extra network calls; confirm acceptable.

**Stop point**: the plan ends here. Waiting for your explicit approval of the "plan"; after the tests are approved, waiting again for your explicit authorization to "implement the feature" — no implementation code is written before that.

```
"""Vendor data-error taxonomy.

A single hierarchy so the routing layer reacts by *behavior*, not by vendor:
every condition where a vendor cannot return usable data derives from
``VendorError``, and the router catches the base types. A new vendor raises
these (or a thin vendor-named subclass) and needs no new ``except`` clause.

    VendorError
    ├── NoMarketDataError          no usable rows (empty result OR stale data)
    ├── VendorUnavailableError     throttled or failed request -> skip to next vendor
    └── VendorNotConfiguredError   missing API key/config -> vendor unavailable

The number of types is the number of distinct router reactions, not the number
of human-describable causes: empty and stale data get identical handling, so
they share ``NoMarketDataError`` and differ only in the free-text ``detail``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations


class VendorError(Exception):
    """Base for any condition where a vendor could not return usable data."""


class NoMarketDataError(VendorError):
    """A vendor returned no usable rows for a symbol (empty result or stale data).

    Carries both the symbol the user requested and the canonical symbol the
    vendor was actually queried with, plus a free-text ``detail``, so callers
    can build a clear message instead of emitting a vendor-specific empty
    string into the data channel.
    """

    def __init__(self, symbol: str, canonical: str | None = None, detail: str = ""):
        self.symbol = symbol
        self.canonical = canonical or symbol
        self.detail = detail
        msg = f"No market data for {symbol!r}"
        if canonical and canonical != symbol:
            msg += f" (queried as {canonical!r})"

```

# FEAT-03 (FR-RPT-01) — Revised Plan (Plan Only)

Status: **not approved**. This revision modifies no files, writes no tests, writes no implementation, installs nothing, and does not commit, push, or change Git config. Branch `CS5351`, commit `d0ca820`, working tree clean (verified). The historical current-name rule is treated as already specified by FR-RPT-01 and RPT-T4; it is not reopened.

## 1. Branch, commit, working-tree status

- Branch: `CS5351` (tracking `origin/CS5351`); no branch created or switched.
- HEAD: `d0ca820925f959163d9fcc731c6376caee7afc75`.
- Working tree: clean.
- Baseline `4cff72b` is present for diff review.

## 2. Completion criteria mapped to FR-RPT-01

| # | Criterion | Requirement link | Checks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C1 | Exactly one Company Background section per consolidated report | FR-RPT-01 | Markdown count = 1; HTML section count = 1 |
| C2 | After the header, before analyst reports | FR-RPT-01 | Position relative to header end and `## I. Analyst Team Reports` / first section |
| C3 | Independent of selected analysts; no Fundamentals Analyst needed | FR-RPT-01 | Run with `selected_analysts` lacking `fundamentals` |
| C4 | Show available name, industry, 1–2 sentence business description; omit missing fields | FR-RPT-01 | Full profile and name-only cases |
| C5 | No eligible fields → unavailable notice, export completes | FR-RPT-01 | Empty profile; final decision still exported |
| C6 | Historical policy: current name explicitly labelled current; undated industry/business not shown as historical | FR-RPT-01 + existing rule | Historical case |
| C7 | Same information in Markdown and requested HTML | FR-RPT-01 | Cross-format equivalence |
| C8 | No agent or model call; reuse data access and export paths | FR-RPT-01 | Model-call counter; no new vendor path |
| C9 | Preserve public imports, CLI behavior, data compatibility, graph behavior, teammates' features | AGENTS.md | Prior offline suite + targeted regressions |

## 3. Actual Python call paths (running vs. saving), corrected

Fact from code: running an analysis and saving its reports are **separate** operations. `propagate()`/CLI streaming do **not** write the report tree; `save_reports`/`_offer_reports` do.

**Run-only path (Python)**
`TradingAgentsGraph.propagate()` (`trading_graph.py:167`) → `_run_graph()` (`:373`) → `create_run_state()` (`:293`) → `Propagator.create_initial_state()` (`propagation.py:13`). Identity resolution happens inside `create_run_state` via `resolve_instrument_context()` (`trading_graph.py:305` → `:117` → `resolve_instrument_identity()` `context.py:61` → `get_company_profile()` `fundamentals.py:169`). Then `_run_graph` → `record_decision()` (`:359`) → `_log_state()` (`:438`) and the memory log. **No report files here.**

**Explicit save path (Python)**
`TradingAgentsGraph.save_reports(final_state, ticker, save_path, html)` (`:277`) → `write_report_tree(...)` (`reporting.py:93`) → optional `render_report(...)` (`report_html.py:249`). `final_state` is supplied by the caller; the exporter currently reads only `final_state` and `run_settings()`. The run's profile is **not** in `final_state` today (only `company_of_interest`, `trade_date`, and the rendered `instrument_context` text are).

**Run-only path (CLI)**
`cli/run.py::run_analysis()` (`:99`) → `graph.create_run_state()` (`:219`) → `stream_run` → merged `final_state` → `graph.record_decision()` (`:353`). **No report files in this block.**

**Explicit save path (CLI)**
`_offer_reports(final_state, graph, ...)` (`:388`/`:426`) → `graph.save_reports(...)` (`:449`) → `write_report_tree(...)`. `display_complete_report(final_state)` (`display.py:383`) is terminal display only, not the consolidated report export.

**Where profile fields come from / are retained / filtered / exported today**
- Source: `yfinance` `Ticker(...).info` via `get_company_profile` (`fundamentals.py:169`).
- Company name/sector/industry/exchange: retained as cleaned strings in `_identity`'s `lru_cache` (`context.py:85`), keyed by ticker, then serialized to the `instrument_context` string. Not stored as structured data in the graph state.
- Business description (`longBusinessSummary`): available in `info` but **not retained or used anywhere**.
- Filtering: `_clean_identity_value` drops empty/placeholder values; historical semantics only via `is_historical`.
- Export: **profile is unused**; the consolidated report has no background section today.

## 4. Design — inputs, no-extra-network reuse, single preparation, compatibility

### 4.1 `company_profile_view` exact inputs

The function takes an **explicit identity mapping and an explicit analysis date**; it performs no I/O and no lookup:

```
company_profile_view(identity: Mapping[str, str], trade_date: str | None) -> CompanyProfileView
```

- `identity`: the same dict already produced by `resolve_instrument_identity` / `_identity` (company_name, industry, business_description, plus unrelated keys ignored).
- `trade_date`: the run's analysis date string from `final_state["trade_date"]`.
- Returns a small immutable view (e.g. dataclass or `TypedDict`): `name: str|None`, `name_is_current: bool`, `industry: str|None`, `business_description: str|None`. Missing/placeholder values become `None`; historical runs yield name-only with `name_is_current=True` and industry/description `None`. The view is ready-to-render (description already trimmed to 1–2 sentences).

How the correct run's data reaches it: the exporter has `ticker = final_state["company_of_interest"]` (or the caller's `ticker`) and `trade_date = final_state["trade_date"]`. The identity is obtained by a `profile_source(identity_lookup)` step below using those exact run values.

### 4.2 Reusing the run's profile without a new network lookup

The `lru_cache` only helps within the same process after a successful lookup; it does not cover old states, cold caches, or a new process. Resolve this with a **prepared-profile provider plus deterministic fallback**, and make identity **retained on the run**:

- **Retain identity on the run (state field).** Have `create_run_state` (via `resolve_instrument_context`) also place the resolved identity mapping into a state key, e.g. `company_identity: dict[str, str]`, and persist it in `_log_state` output and in the saved state. Both entry paths (`propagate` and CLI) already go through `create_run_state`, so a freshly run analysis carries its own profile with **zero** additional lookups at export time.
- **Export-time source resolution (deterministic, ordered):**
  1. If `final_state` contains `company_identity` (fresh run, saved state with the field), use it — **no lookup**.
  2. Else, if the state carries a ticker and the process already resolved it (cache hit), reuse `resolve_instrument_identity(ticker)` — **no network** because `lru_cache` hits.
  3. Else (old state without the field, cold cache, or new process export): use the **deterministic, network-free fallback** — derive a name-only identity from what the old state reliably holds. Old states always contain `company_of_interest` (ticker) and may contain `instrument_context`. To avoid a network call, the fallback parses the previously rendered `instrument_context` identity text when present; if that is absent, the view is **empty** and the exporter emits the unavailable notice. **The exporter never triggers a vendor lookup.**
- This makes export behavior a pure function of stored run data: identical input → identical output, including in a separate process.

**Revised frozen paths.** To retain identity at run time I must touch `src/tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py`, `src/tradingagents/graph/propagation.py`, and `src/tradingagents/agents/state.py` (add an optional state key). I no longer propose these as frozen. **Tradeoff:** this widens the editable set and changes the saved state/log shape (additive only), but it is the only way to guarantee "no extra network lookup for old states/new processes" while keeping deterministic exports. `dataflows/vendors/yahoo/fundamentals.py` and `dataflows/date_window.py` stay frozen (read-only reuse). If you prefer to keep those three files frozen instead, the fallback degrades to **unavailable notice** for old states/cold caches and a name-only parse when `instrument_context` exists — I flag this as an unresolved decision (§9, D1).

### 4.3 Single preparation, shared by Markdown and HTML

Prepare eligible background once per export in `write_report_tree` and pass the **same prepared object** to both renderers:

Proposed call flow:

```
write_report_tree(final_state, ticker, save_path, settings, html)
  background = build_company_background(final_state, ticker)   # context.py: profile_source + company_profile_view
  _write_markdown(..., background)                              # reporting.py renders from `background`
  render_report(ticker, final_state, settings, parts, background)  # report_html.py renders from the same `background`
```

- `build_company_background(final_state, ticker)` owns source resolution (§4.2) and returns a `CompanyProfileView` (possibly empty). No rendering, no I/O beyond the ordered deterministic source rules.
- Markdown and HTML each render from this single view; neither re-derives or re-looks-up.
- **Interface compatibility:** `write_report_tree(...)` signature is unchanged. `render_report(...)` gains a **keyword-only optional** `background: CompanyProfileView | None = None`; when omitted (existing callers/tests) it renders nothing extra, so public/on-disk behavior is unchanged for old calls. `save_reports` signature unchanged; it forwards `final_state` as today and `write_report_tree` performs preparation.

It also sells networking gear."}`, today's date; final decision present | Exactly one background section, after header / before `## I.`; shows name, industry, both sentences; identical across formats; both entry paths |

# FEAT-03 (FR-RPT-01) — Consolidated Final Plan (Plan Only)

**Status: not approved.** No files modified, no tests written, no implementation written, nothing installed, no commit/push, no Git config change. Branch `CS5351`, HEAD `d0ca820`, working tree clean (verified this session). The historical current-name rule is fixed by FR-RPT-01 and RPT-T4 and is not reopened.

## 1. Branch, commit, working-tree

- Branch: `CS5351` (tracking `origin/CS5351`); no branch created or switched.
- HEAD: `d0ca820925f959163d9fcc731c6376caee7afc75`.
- Working tree: clean; baseline `4cff72b` available for diff review.

## 2. Completion criteria mapped to FR-RPT-01

| # | Criterion | Link | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C1 | Exactly one Company Background section per consolidated report | FR-RPT-01 | Markdown count = 1; HTML section count = 1 |
| C2 | After header, before the numbered analyst sections | FR-RPT-01 | Position vs. header end and `## I.` / first section |
| C3 | Independent of analyst selection; no Fundamentals Analyst needed | FR-RPT-01 | Run with `selected_analysts` lacking `fundamentals` |
| C4 | Show available name, industry, 1–2 sentence business description; omit missing | FR-RPT-01 | Full + name-only cases |
| C5 | No eligible fields → unavailable notice, export completes | FR-RPT-01 | Empty/absent `company_identity` |
| C6 | Historical: current name labelled current; undated industry/business not shown as history | FR-RPT-01 (existing rule) | Historical case |
| C7 | Same information in Markdown and requested HTML | FR-RPT-01 | Cross-format equivalence |
| C8 | No agent/model call; no second identity lookup; reuse existing data access & export | FR-RPT-01 | Stubbed lookup count = 1 per run; model-call = 0 |
| C9 | Preserve public imports, CLI behavior, data compat, graph behavior, teammates' features | AGENTS.md | `python -m pytest -q test/offline` + targeted regressions |

## 3. Actual call paths (running vs. saving)

Running and saving are separate operations; running does not write the report tree.

**Run initialization (both entry points)**
`create_run_state(company_name, trade_date, asset_type, portfolio)` (`trading_graph.py:293`) calls `resolve_instrument_context(company_name, asset_type, trade_date)` (`:305` → `:117`), which calls `resolve_instrument_identity(ticker)` (`context.py:61` → cached `_identity` → `get_company_profile` `fundamentals.py:169`) and renders the `instrument_context` string. **This is the only identity lookup.** `propagate()` (`:167`) → `_run_graph()` (`:373`) and the CLI `run_analysis()` (`cli/run.py:99` → `create_run_state` `:219`) both start from `create_run_state`, then `record_decision()`/`_log_state()` (`:359`/`:438`).

**Explicit save (Python)** `save_reports(final_state, ticker, save_path, html)` (`:277`) → `write_report_tree(...)` (`reporting.py:93`) → optional `render_report(...)` (`report_html.py:249`).

**Explicit save (CLI)** `_offer_reports(...)` (`cli/run.py:426`; called `:388`) → `graph.save_reports(...)` (`:449`) → `write_report_tree(...)`. `display_complete_report` is terminal-only, not export.

**Current profile handling:** name/sector/industry/exchange are cleaned in `_identity` (lru_cache) and serialized only into `instrument_context` text; `longBusinessSummary` is available in `info` but not retained; export uses **no** profile today.

## 4. Design (proposed, final)

### 4.1 Retain profile at run initialization (single lookup, no second lookup)
- Extend the cached `_identity` to also retain the cleaned `business_description` from `info["longBusinessSummary"]` (same `_clean_identity_value` filter). No extra vendor call.
- Preserve `resolve_instrument_context(...) -> str` **interface and behavior exactly** (still returns only the context string).
- `create_run_state` obtains the identity **once** for this run and returns *both* the context string and the retained profile. Concretely: `create_run_state` calls the existing identity path once (e.g. `_identity`/`resolve_instrument_identity`), passes that same mapping to `build_instrument_context` for the unchanged context string, and puts a cleaned, snapshot copy into the new optional state key `company_identity`. No second lookup is introduced; the retained value is the same mapping already used for the context.
- This happens for both entry points because both start from `create_run_state`.

### 4.2 Export reads only stored run data
- `write_report_tree` reads `company_identity` (and `trade_date`) from `final_state` only. **No** export-time cache access, identity lookup, or `instrument_context` parsing.
- If `company_identity` is absent or empty → unavailable notice; export completes; no network/cache access.
- Old states without the key remain readable and get the notice (or historical name-only when the key is present from a run).

### 4.3 Prepare once, share both formats
Proposed flow:
```
write_report_tree(final_state, ticker, save_path, settings, html)
  view = build_company_background(final_state)          # pure: reads only stored data
  markdown = _header(...) + _company_background_markdown(view) + sections
  render_report(ticker, final_state, settings, parts, background=view)   # HTML from same view
```
- `build_company_background(final_state) -> CompanyProfileView` is pure and deterministic (no I/O). Returns `name`, `name_is_current`, `industry`, `business_description` (all `None` when absent), or an empty view when no eligible field.
- `company_profile_view(identity, trade_date)` remains an internal pure helper used by `build_company_background`.

**`render_report` interface and existing direct callers.** Signature becomes `render_report(ticker, final_state, settings, parts, *, background=None)` (new keyword-only, default `None`). Existing direct callers—`write_report_tree` (the only in-repo caller)—will pass `background=view`; if `background is None` (any test or third-party direct call), the page renders exactly as today with **no** background section, so current HTML tests/behavior are unchanged.

### 4.4 Presentation and description trimming
- Independent "Company Background" section before the numbered sections (not numbered into I–V, not in the HTML contents nav). English labels consistent with the exporter (e.g. `## Company Background`, fields `Name`, `Industry`, `Business`).
- Historical run: name shown with an explicit "current name" label; industry/business omitted.
- Description uses the source `longBusinessSummary` text verbatim; **no model call**.
- **Sentence-trimming rule (proposed):** normalize whitespace; split after `.!?` followed by whitespace/end; keep the first 2 sentences; if the first sentence alone exceeds ~320 characters, truncate at the last word boundary within that limit and append `…`. **Limitations:** abbreviations/decimals/initials can cause mis-splits; the 1–2 sentence result is a bounded presentation of the source, not a semantic summary.

```
def _prompt_text(prompt) -> str:
    if isinstance(prompt, str):
        return prompt
    parts = []
    for message in prompt:
        content = message.content if hasattr(message, "content") else str(message)
        parts.append(str(content))
    return "\n".join(parts)
```

```
    def _llm_type(self) -> str:
        return "scripted"

    def bind_tools(self, tools, **kwargs):
        return self.model_copy(update={"tools": tuple(tools)})

    def with_structured_output(self, schema, **kwargs):
        if not self.structured:
            raise NotImplementedError
        return RunnableLambda(lambda _: self._count() or STRUCTURED[schema])

    def _count(self) -> None:
        self.calls.append(1)
        if len(self.calls) == self.fail_at:
            raise RuntimeError("provider unavailable")

    def _generate(self, messages, stop=None, run_manager=None, **kwargs) -> ChatResult:
        self._count()
        if self.tools:
            import threading
            import time
            self.threads.add(threading.current_thread().name)
            time.sleep(0.05)   # long enough for concurrent analysts to overlap
        if self.tools and not isinstance(messages[-1], ToolMessage):
            calls = [{"name": t.name, "id": f"call_{i}",
                      "args": {k: v for k, v in ARGS.items()

def _graph(tmp_path, monkeypatch, model, debug=False, **config):
    cfg = copy.deepcopy(DEFAULT_CONFIG)
    cfg.update(results_dir=str(tmp_path / "results"), data_cache_dir=str(tmp_path / "cache"),
               memory_log_path=str(tmp_path / "log.md"), **config)
    monkeypatch.setattr(trading_graph, "create_tier_client", lambda config, tier, **k: _Client(model))
    return trading_graph.TradingAgentsGraph(config=cfg, debug=debug)


@pytest.mark.unit
@pytest.mark.parametrize("structured", [False, True], ids=["free-text", "structured"])
def test_a_full_run_reaches_a_logged_decision(tmp_path, monkeypatch, offline, structured):
    graph = _graph(tmp_path, monkeypatch, ScriptedModel(structured=structured))

    state, signal = graph.propagate("NVDA", TRADE_DATE)

    assert signal == state["final_rating"] == "Overweight"
    for key in ("market_report", "sentiment_report", "news_report", "fundamentals_report",
                "options_report", "investment_plan", "trader_investment_plan",
                "final_trade_decision"):
        assert state[key].strip(), key
    tool_methods = {"get_stock_data", "get_indicators", "get_news", "get_global_news",
                    "get_macro_indicators", "get_prediction_markets", "get_fundamentals",
                    "get_balance_sheet", "get_cashflow", "get_income_statement",
                    "get_insider_transactions", "get_option_chain", "ohlcv"}
    assert offline == tool_methods
    assert [e["rating"] for e in graph.memory_log.load_entries()] == ["Overweight"]
```

Full contents:

```python
"""FEAT-03 / FR-RPT-01: a Company Background section in the consolidated report.

The report must carry one factual introduction drawn from the run's retained
company profile, between the header and the numbered analyst sections, offered
in both Markdown and the requested HTML. It is found without the Fundamentals
Analyst and with no extra agent or model call. A run's profile is captured once
at initialization (the single existing identity lookup) and kept on the run
state as ``company_identity``; the exporter reads only stored run data, never
the network or the identity cache.

These tests pin the required observable behaviour:
- initialization retains the cleaned profile (name, industry, description)
  from the one lookup and does not bypass ``resolve_instrument_context``;
- the retained profile survives the graph-state flow into final-state export;
- the profile is persisted in the run log;
- both formats show the same data, and the section sits in the required place;
- historical runs label the current name and omit undated details;
- missing profiles show an unavailable notice and still export;
- no export path triggers a second lookup, cache access or model call.

No implementation of this feature exists yet, so most cases are expected to
fail until FEAT-03 lands.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import copy
import json

import pytest

from offline.test_graph_end_to_end import ScriptedModel, _graph as _e2e_graph
from tradingagents.agents import context
from tradingagents.dataflows.date_window import get_current_date
from tradingagents.graph import trading_graph
from tradingagents.reporting import write_report_tree

TODAY = get_current_date()
PAST = "2024-05-10"

PROFILE_FIELDS = {"company_name", "industry", "business_description"}

FULL_INFO = {
    "longName": "NVIDIA Corporation",
    "industry": "Semiconductors",
    "longBusinessSummary": (
        "NVIDIA Corporation provides graphics and compute solutions worldwide. "
        "The company also sells networking equipment and software."
    ),
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Helpers
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

class _ProfileSpy:
    """Stands in for the single identity lookup and counts its invocations."""

    def __init__(self, info):
        self.info = info
        self.calls = 0

    def __call__(self, ticker):
        self.calls += 1
        return dict(self.info)

def _spy(monkeypatch, info):
    """Replace the run's single profile lookup; clear the cache for isolation."""
    spy = _ProfileSpy(info)
    monkeypatch.setattr(context, "get_company_profile", spy)
    context._identity.cache_clear()
    return spy

def _forbid_lookups(monkeypatch):
    """Make any identity lookup or cache access during export fail loudly."""
    def _forbidden(*a, **k):
        raise AssertionError("the export path must not look up or cache identity")

    monkeypatch.setattr(context, "get_company_profile", _forbidden)
    monkeypatch.setattr(context, "_identity", _forbidden)

def _selected_graph(tmp_path, monkeypatch, model, selected):
    """A graph with an explicit analyst selection, patched like the e2e harness."""
    from tradingagents.default_config import DEFAULT_CONFIG

    class _LocalClient:
        def __init__(self, m):
            self.model = m

        def get_llm(self):
            return self.model

    cfg = copy.deepcopy(DEFAULT_CONFIG)
    cfg.update(results_dir=str(tmp_path / "results"), data_cache_dir=str(tmp_path / "cache"),
               memory_log_path=str(tmp_path / "log.md"))
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        trading_graph, "create_tier_client", lambda config, tier, **k: _LocalClient(model)
    )
    return trading_graph.TradingAgentsGraph(selected, config=cfg)

def _export(tmp_path, state, ticker="NVDA", html=True, subdir="r"):
    out = write_report_tree(state, ticker, tmp_path / subdir, settings={}, html=html)
    markdown = out.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    page = (
        (tmp_path / subdir / "complete_report.html").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        if html else ""
    )
    return markdown, page

def _block(markdown: str) -> str:
    """The text between the header and the first numbered section."""
    head, sep, _rest = markdown.partition("## I.")
    assert sep, "the report has no numbered analyst section to bound the background"
    return head

def _section_count(markdown: str) -> int:
    return sum(
        1 for line in markdown.splitlines()
        if line.strip().lower() == "## company background"
    )

def _export_state(**overrides):
    """A completed run's final state for export-only cases."""
    state = {
        "company_of_interest": "NVDA",
        "trade_date": TODAY,
        "asset_type": "stock",
        "market_report": "MARKET REPORT BODY",
        "news_report": "NEWS REPORT BODY",
        "investment_debate_state": {
            "bull_history": "", "bear_history": "", "history": "",
            "current_response": "", "count": 0,
        },
        "investment_plan": "PLAN",
        "trader_investment_plan": "TRADE",
        "risk_debate_state": {
            "aggressive_history": "", "conservative_history": "", "neutral_history": "",
            "history": "", "latest_speaker": "", "current_aggressive_response": "",
            "current_conservative_response": "", "current_neutral_response": "", "count": 0,
        },
        "final_trade_decision": "**Rating**: Overweight\n\nThe final decision stands.",
    }
    state.update(overrides)
    return state
```

```
def _offer_reports(final_state, graph, ticker, save=None, show=None, html=None):
    """Save the report tree and show it; ``save``/``show``/``html`` answer the questions when given.

    A saved report includes the HTML page unless ``html`` is False. Someone
    answering the save question at the prompt is also asked about the page and
    offered to open it; a run whose flags answer the save question asks neither.
    """
    asked = save is None
    if asked:
        save = typer.prompt("Save report?", default="Y").strip().upper() in ("Y", "YES", "")
    if save:
        # Under results_dir, not the working directory: in Docker the working
        # directory is inside the container and the report goes with it, while
        # results_dir is the mounted volume the rest of the run already writes to.
        save_path = graph.default_report_path(ticker)
        if asked:   # someone at the prompt may pick another folder
            save_path = Path(typer.prompt(
                "Save path (press Enter for default)", default=str(save_path)
            ).strip())
        if html is None:
            html = _yes("Also save it as an HTML page?") if asked else True
        saved = False
        try:
            report_file = graph.save_reports(final_state, ticker, save_path, html=html)
            saved = True
            console.print(f"\n[green]✓ Report saved to:[/green] {save_path.resolve()}")
            console.print(f"  [dim]Complete report:[/dim] {report_file.name}")
        except Exception as e:
            console.print(f"[red]Error saving report: {e}[/red]")
        if saved and html:
            page = (save_path / "complete_report.html").resolve()
            console.print(f"  [dim]HTML report:[/dim] {page.name}")
            if asked:
                _open_page(page)

    if show is None:
        show = typer.prompt("\nDisplay full report on screen?", default="Y").strip().upper() in ("Y", "YES", "")
    if show:
        display_complete_report(final_state)
```

```
def get_category_for_method(method: str) -> str:
    """Get the category that contains the specified method."""
    for category, info in TOOLS_CATEGORIES.items():
        if method in info["tools"]:
            return category
    raise ValueError(f"Method '{method}' not found in any category")


def get_vendor(category: str, method: str = None) -> str:
    """Get the configured vendor for a data category or specific tool method.
    Tool-level configuration takes precedence over category-level.
    """
    config = get_config()

    # Check tool-level configuration first (if method provided)
    if method:
        tool_vendors = config.get("tool_vendors", {})
        if method in tool_vendors:
            return tool_vendors[method]

    # Fall back to category-level configuration
    return config.get("data_vendors", {}).get(category, "default")


def vendor_unavailable(method: str, error: Exception) -> str:
    """What a call returns when every vendor was throttled or unreachable."""
    return (
        f"DATA_UNAVAILABLE: no configured vendor could serve {method} right now "
        f"({error}). This says nothing about the instrument; report the "
        f"data as unavailable and do not estimate or fabricate values."
    )


def no_data_available(error: NoMarketDataError) -> str:
    """What a call returns when every vendor that answered had no usable data."""
    resolved = "" if error.canonical == error.symbol else f" (resolved to '{error.canonical}')"
    # Surface the typed error's detail (e.g. "latest row is 2025-06-11 ...
    # stale") so the agent sees the specific reason — invalid symbol, no
    # coverage, or stale data — not just a generic "unavailable".
    reason = f" ({error.detail})" if error.detail else ""
    return (
        f"NO_DATA_AVAILABLE: No usable market data for '{error.symbol}'{resolved} from "
        f"any configured vendor{reason}. The symbol may be invalid, delisted, "
        f"not covered, or the vendor returned stale data. Do not estimate or "
        f"fabricate values — report that data is unavailable for this symbol."
    )
```

2. **Stronger per-format assertions.** Full profile asserts name+industry+`DESCRIPTION_TWO` in both formats; name-only asserts `Industry` label and content absent in both; historical asserts `current` label and absence of industry/description in both Markdown and HTML; the historical-no-name case asserts the notice with neither undated field leaked; all sentence cases assert both formats.
3. **Real section extraction.** `_background_markdown` (regex, asserts exactly one `## Company Background` bounded by the next `## `) and `_background_html` (asserts exactly one block; section or heading-anchored) plus `_markdown_sections`/`_html_text`. Placement asserted via heading order (background first, before `I. Analyst Team Reports`) and HTML position.
4. **Vendors stubbed.** Graph-run tests now use the real `offline` fixture (stubs every `router.VENDOR_METHODS` vendor, `load_ohlcv`, sentiment feeds, `yf.Ticker`). Confirmed no network/OSError lines in graph runs; the earlier yfinance/polymarket attempts are gone.
5. **Fixed clock and cache hygiene.** Autouse `_fixed_clock` patches `date_window.get_current_date` and `trading_graph.get_current_date` to `TODAY`; autouse `_clean_identity_cache` clears `context._identity` before and after every test. Fixed dates: `TODAY = "2026-06-15"`, `PAST = "2024-05-10"`.
6. **Tightened init lookup.** `test_initialization_reuses_the_cached_profile_without_a_second_lookup` asserts `spy.calls == 1` after a direct `resolve_instrument_context` **then** `create_run_state`, and that the context string equals the run's `instrument_context`.

## Summary

I added regression tests only, to `test/offline/test_company_background.py`. Implementation (`src/`) and documentation were not modified this turn; the `src/` and `docs/` entries in `git status` are from the prior implementation turn and remain untouched now.

### Proposed correction design (to implement after approval)

- **Issue 1 — Markdown/HTML literal parity.** Today `reporting.py` interpolates raw profile text into Markdown (`- Name: {name}`), while `report_html.py` does `escape(...)`. To make both show the same visible *source* text, both renderers must present the profile text literally: escape Markdown-significant characters (at minimum `\ * _ [ ] < > & `` ` `` and leading list/heading markers) for the Markdown field values — or render the field values through a common literal-escaping helper before interpolation — so `Example *Group*` appears as literal asterisks in both. HTML already escapes; Markdown needs equivalent escaping so emphasis/links/tags are not produced. One shared "literal text" preparation step in the once-per-export background keeps the two formats identical.
- **Issue 2 — optional state field.** Declare `company_identity` as `NotRequired[...]` (or `total=False` for that key) in `AgentState` so it lands in `__optional_keys__` while `Propagator` still writes it (`{}` default). Graph retention and legacy-state export are unchanged; only the schema contract becomes genuinely optional.
- **Issue 3 — respect the `resolve_instrument_context` hook while keeping one lookup.** `create_run_state` should call `self.resolve_instrument_context(...)` for the context string (preserving overrides), and separately obtain the profile from the same single vendor resolution. To avoid a second vendor call, the profile is read from the already-cached `resolve_instrument_identity(...)` (a cache hit after the context path resolved it), then `retained_company_identity(...)`. #### part 1 — text

Now I understand the design constraints for correction 3:

- A **custom** `resolve_instrument_context` override means `self.resolve_instrument_context` no longer equals the default; it may not populate the `_identity` cache. So after calling the hook, reading `resolve_instrument_identity` would perform a lookup (cache miss) — but that's the *one* needed vendor lookup, and the test asserts `spy.calls == 1`. Good.
- For the **default** implementation, calling `self.resolve_instrument_context(...)` already resolves identity (populating the cache), then `resolve_instrument_identity` is a cache hit — still one vendor request.
- **Failed lookup path:** `resolve_instrument_identity` returns `{}` on failure and `_identity` is **not** cached (lru_cache doesn't cache exceptions). If the default hook already attempted and failed, a second call would **re-attempt** the vendor → duplicate request. The requirement says "a failed resolution must not accidentally trigger an immediate duplicate request."

So the safe design: resolve identity **once** in `create_run_state`, use it both for the stored profile and to avoid re-resolving, while still honoring a custom hook. The cleanest way: 
1. Call `self.resolve_instrument_context(...)` for the context string (honors override).
2. Reuse the **already-cached** identity if present; otherwise resolve once. But on default path with a failed lookup, there's no cached value.

To avoid the duplicate-on-failure problem while reusing a single resolution, I'll resolve identity **first** into a local, then:
- If `resolve_instrument_context` is the **default** method (not overridden), build the context from that same identity (no second resolve).
- If it **is** overridden, call the override for the context string AND use the identity we resolved for the profile.

But that would make an overridden hook coexist with our own resolve → potentially a second vendor request if the override also looks up. However, the test's custom hook does **not** look up; it just returns a string, and asserts `spy.calls == 1`. If we resolve identity once for the profile and call the hook (no lookup), total = 1. 

For the default (non-overridden) case: resolving identity once + building context from it = 1 lookup, no hook re-resolve.

For the failed-lookup case: one `resolve_instrument_identity` returns `{}` (failed, uncached). We must not call it again. If default, we build context from `{}` (no second resolve). If overridden, we call the hook (the hook may or may not resolve; that's the user's code) but we do **not** call `resolve_instrument_identity` a second time ourselves.

So the design: resolve once into `identity`; decide whether the method is overridden; then:
- default: `context = build_instrument_context(... identity ...)`
- overridden: `context = self.resolve_instrument_context(...)` (honor it)

That gives exactly one `resolve_instrument_identity` call in all our code paths, honors overrides, and never duplicates on failure. Detecting "overridden": compare `self.resolve_instrument_context.__func__` to `TradingAgentsGraph.resolve_instrument_context`. For a lambda assigned to the instance, `__func__` won't exist — treat as overridden.

This needs no test or design change beyond what's approved (the approved custom-hook test asserts hook called with `(ticker, asset_type, trade_date)`, its result used, and `spy.calls == 1`). Let me verify the approved test's exact expectations again.

# FEAT-03 Implementation-Review Corrections — Report

The three corrections are implemented. The approved test file is unchanged (blob `1023b4c964fa96bf7d5f734f1f97632df58c0b43`, confirmed after edits). No implementation design or test change was required beyond what was approved; correction 3 fit the approved custom-hook test without modification.

## Correction diff (source)

**1. `src/tradingagents/reporting.py` — format-specific escaping; raw text kept in shared view**

The shared view from `build_company_background` already holds raw source text; only the Markdown renderer escapes:
```python
import re
...
_MD_SPECIAL = re.compile(r"([\\`*_\[\]<>])")

def _md_escape(value: str) -> str:
    return _MD_SPECIAL.sub(r"\\\1", value)

def _company_background_markdown(view: dict) -> str:
    lines = []
    if view.get("name"):
        suffix = " (current name)" if view["name_is_current"] else ""
        lines.append(f"- Name: {_md_escape(view['name'])}{suffix}")
    if view.get("industry"):
        lines.append(f"- Industry: {_md_escape(view['industry'])}")
    if view.get("business_description"):
        lines.append(f"- Business: {_md_escape(view['business_description'])}")
    ...
```
HTML renderer unchanged — it keeps its `escape(...)`; no Markdown-escaped value is passed to HTML.

**2. `src/tradingagents/agents/state.py` — genuinely optional field**
```python
from typing_extensions import NotRequired, TypedDict
...
    company_identity: NotRequired[
        Annotated[
            dict,
            "Retained cleaned company profile (name, industry, business description) for the report",
        ]
    ]
```
`Propagator` still writes `company_identity` (`{}` default), so retention/persistence are unchanged; the schema now lists it in `__optional_keys__`.

**3. `src/tradingagents/graph/trading_graph.py` — honour the hook, one resolution, no retry on failure**
```python
trade_date = _validate_trade_date(trade_date)
identity = resolve_instrument_identity(company_name)
if self._has_custom_instrument_context():
    instrument_context = self.resolve_instrument_context(company_name, asset_type, trade_date)
else:
    instrument_context = build_instrument_context(company_name, asset_type, identity, trade_date)
return self.propagator.create_initial_state(
    ..., instrument_context=instrument_context,
    company_identity=retained_company_identity(identity),
)

def _has_custom_instrument_context(self) -> bool:
    method = self.resolve_instrument_context
    default = TradingAgentsGraph.resolve_instrument_context
    return getattr(method, "__func__", None) is not default
```
Design rationale (verified): the default path uses the single `resolve_instrument_identity` result for both the context and the profile (one lookup, no re-resolve). A custom override is called once for the context string, while the profile comes from the single resolution. On a **failed** lookup, `resolve_instrument_identity` returns `{}` and the lru cache does not store the exception, so the code must not call it again — it doesn’t: it calls `resolve_instrument_identity` exactly once and then builds context from that `{}` (default) or calls the user’s hook (custom). A probe confirmed one vendor attempt and no duplicate.

## 2. Implementation summary (mapped to FR-RPT-01)

- **Profile retention (single lookup):** `_identity` cleans and keeps `company_name`, `industry`, `business_description` (from `longBusinessSummary`). `create_run_state` resolves identity once, retains only those cleaned fields in the optional state field `company_identity`, and reuses that one resolution for the retained profile. A custom `resolve_instrument_context` override is still honoured for the context string; a failed resolution is not retried (one vendor attempt; no duplicate).
- **Historical filtering:** `company_profile_view` shows the analysis-date-appropriate view; for a historical run only the current name is shown, explicitly labelled current, and undated industry/description are omitted.
- **Missing-data handling:** absent/empty profile → all-None view → an unavailable notice in the report; the export completes with the analysis and final decision intact.
- **Format consistency:** raw source text is kept in the shared view; `write_report_tree` prepares it once and passes the same view to Markdown and HTML. Markdown escapes Markdown-significant characters; HTML escapes for HTML — both show the same visible source text.
- **Persistence:** `_log_state` records `company_identity`. Verified in the acceptance log (full raw description stored).
- **Compatibility:** `company_identity` is declared `NotRequired`; `render_report` gains keyword-only `background=None` (direct callers unchanged); old states without the field export with the notice; HTML CSP/safe rendering preserved.

These retrospective annotations are outside the historical transcript. They were drafted with assistance from the separate review chat and explicitly accepted by the student before insertion. They are not messages from the original OpenCode session and do not constitute a final review verdict.

1. **Initial planning and plan revisions.** Messages `msg_20316d1f60013fJ2XWgrnSGnsP` (the opening instruction, including the request for Chinese replies), `msg_20317b893001skoSN0waRoAFHa` (the Chinese plan, translated), `msg_2031c00e5001H1fw5Z0pZQSNRF` and `msg_2031e68a5001K2V5thclJdV7Ra` (English switch and plan revisions).

   I used a separate review chat to examine OpenCode’s initial plans before allowing implementation. The review identified unclear profile inputs and inconsistencies between deterministic export and cache-based fallback. Based on these explanations, I requested revisions and accepted retaining structured company data during run initialization, with no lookup during export. This gave me a clearer basis for reviewing the proposed file changes, compatibility rules and tests.

2. **Original test approval.** Messages `msg_20325ea9f001YDLM7m4xeB7nO1` (review of the test diff, not approved) and `msg_2032b08c2001f5bLN1gSnhL4Qs` (approval at blob `821e88d24eae95fcd7f01bf094fb23a90bff52b2`).

   I approved the original tests only after the revised test file covered profile initialization, retention through the graph, persistence, both export entry points and both output formats. OpenCode reported expected failures because the feature had not yet been implemented. With assistance from the review chat, I distinguished these expected failures from gaps in test coverage. I then authorized implementation against the identified test version.

3. **Requests to strengthen insufficient tests.** Message `msg_20325ea9f001YDLM7m4xeB7nO1` (six specific strengthening gaps).

   The first test draft did not fully demonstrate the promised behavior. The separate review chat identified missing coverage of the actual CLI and Python export entries, incomplete HTML assertions and insufficient offline setup. I forwarded these findings to OpenCode and required test-only revisions before implementation. The revised tests checked generated files, historical filtering in both formats, fixed dates and cache isolation. This made the acceptance evidence more closely match the requirement.

4. **Implementation review identifying three defects.** Message `msg_203317050001gJe0QyG1Ggqc7C` (Markdown/HTML literal parity, required-vs-optional state field, bypassed `resolve_instrument_context`).

   The three implementation defects were identified and independently probed by the separate review chat, rather than discovered independently by me. They concerned literal-text differences between Markdown and HTML, a supposedly optional field declared as required, and initialization bypassing the existing context method. I used the review explanations to request focused regression tests before corrections. This showed me that passing the initial suite did not establish every compatibility and presentation claim.

5. **Approval of added regression tests and correction work.** Messages `msg_20336b65f001TsJaQbS4CRQHGE` (regression tests approved at blob `1023b4c964fa96bf7d5f734f1f97632df58c0b43`) and `msg_20347dbd8001vw578VuuTHWLkz` (delivery handoff request).
